 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 22-09-2022 at about 12:00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-L-885, carefully, cautiously and by observing traffic rules, near Saibaba Temple, NH-44, Devanahalli, Bengaluru District.

At that time, all of a sudden a Ford Fiesta car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413, driven by its driver at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger to human life, came and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Manasa Hospital, Devanahalli, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as agriculture labour and was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

The Vijayapura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore,
it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing Reg. No. KA-03- MU-1413 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further, it has sought Chandrappa .B.V vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37318514/
2 permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.

The respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the above contentions, nor it has produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, who was taking turn on Bengaluru-Hyderabad road and due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in his cross-examination that, the said accident has taken place due to his self rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle and there was no fault on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU- 1413.

near Saibaba Temple, NH-44, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to dashing of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413 to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-43-L-885 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others,
reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."

15. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.1 First Information Report and Ex.P.2 first information statement of the complainant.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly provided by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.9 wound certificate and Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 and 12 follow-up records (total 2), Ex.P.13 MRI scan reports, Ex.P.21 inpatient file, Ex.P.22 out-patient file, Ex.P.23 clinical notes and Ex.P.24 x-rays (total 3) it clearly reveals that,
the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered fracture neck of femur of right hip, L1 vertebral body, fracture 7 th and 8th rib, fracture medial end of right clavicle and multiple infarct of occipital parietal lobe.
The same is deposed by P.W.3, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.1, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

20. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ford Fiesta Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture neck of femur of right hip, L1 vertebral body, fracture 7th and 8th rib, fracture medial end of right clavicle and multiple infarct of occipital parietal lobe and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is mentioned as 65 years.
Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.9, 10, 13 and 21, his age is mentioned as 65 years.
On the other hand, in the instant case, the age of the petitioner, as on the date of accident, is not specifically denied or seriously disputed by the respondent No.1.
Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 65 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture neck of femur of right hip, L1 vertebral body, fracture 7th and 8th rib, fracture medial end of right clavicle and multiple infarct of occipital parietal lobe.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 67% physical disability of lower limb and 23% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.9 wound certificate and Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 and 12 follow-up records (total 2), Ex.P.13 MRI scan reports,
Ex.P.21 inpatient file, Ex.P.22 outpatient file, Ex.P.23 clinical notes and Ex.P.24 x-rays (total 3)
clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But,

sentences.text: it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 22-09-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 14-03-2024, which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the injury No.2 to 4 are united, the petitioner has undergone complete treatment, there is no fracture at the knee and ankle of the petitioner, the muscle power of the petitioner is normal and the petitioner can do desk work with difficulties.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as an agriculture labour and was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as agriculture labour and was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 65 years is 7.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.11,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 53 medical bills, as per Ex.P.14.

iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
fracture neck of femur of right hip, L1 vertebral body, fracture 7th and 8th rib, fracture medial end of right clavicle and multiple infarct of occipital parietal lobe.

As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary,
the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 17 days from 22-09-2022 to 08-10-2022, in Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.3, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be Chandrappa .B.V vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37318514/

As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 17 days in Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 17 = Rs.17,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Koramangala, Avathi, Devanahalli Taluk,

Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 17 days as in-patient at Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore,
Rs.15,500 x 3 = Rs.46,500/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 65 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture neck of femur of right hip, L1 vertebral body, fracture 7th and 8th rib, fracture medial end of right clavicle and multiple infarct of occipital parietal lobe.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injury sustained by him in the said accident.
Even, the P.W.3 has not stated anything with respect to same.
The P.W.3 in his cross-examination has admitted that, the petitioner has undergone complete treatment.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

22. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

To establish the same the petitioner has produced true copy of reply given by the respondent No.2/owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.6.

As per the said document, the driver of offending vehicle by name Gajendra D.M. S/o K.P.
Munegowda/respondent No.2 was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA4320050000617 to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was insured by respondent No.1 insurance company, vide Policy No.2311101148006900000, valid from 05-01-2022 to 04-01- 2023.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-03-MU-1413 the said accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,21,277/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.10,21,277/- (Rupees ten lakh twenty one thousand two hundred and seventy seven only) with interest at the rate of 6%

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Vijayapura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c)
and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 22-09-2022 at about 12.00 p.m.,
near Saibaba Temple, NH-44, Devanahalli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Ford Fiesta Car, bearing Reg. No. KA-03- MU-1413 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MU-1413 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to his father, there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.

17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
19.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
On the other hand, in the instant case, the age of the petitioner, as on the date of accident, is not specifically denied or seriously disputed by the respondent No.1.
Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 65 years.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as agriculture labour and was earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
